```{r cleaning parent report data}
census_data<-clean_names(census_data)



#First let's get rid of the screened out people

data_clean<- census_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(status=="Submitted") %>%
  dplyr::filter(by_clicking_on_the_i_agree_button_i_certify_that_i_have_read_the_information_and_consent_form_i_voluntarily_and_freely_consent_to_participate_in_this_research_project== "I agree") %>%
  dplyr::filter(has_your_child_been_diagnosed_with_a_speech_disorder_or_a_language_delay== "No")

#Now let's select only the columns of data that we need

columns_drop<- c(2,3,4, 9:17, 21, 22, 25, 28, 31, 71:86, 92, 103, 114, 120, 121, 122, 128, 136, 140, 141, 143, 144, 146, 150, 151, 153, 154, 156, 160, 161, 163, 164, 166,176, 170, 171, 173, 174, 180, 181, 183:185)
             

data_clean<- data_clean %>%
  dplyr::select(-all_of(columns_drop))

#Now let's clean the column names from the very long ones to ones easy to call in the environment by using the csv file I created containing the survey expost names cleaned from R and shorter manageable names I would like for them to be called

data_clean <- data_clean %>%
  rename(!!!setNames(column_clean_names$old_names,
                     column_clean_names$new_names))


#Now let's get dates into the correct format 
data_clean$survey_date<- as.Date(data_clean$survey_date)
data_clean$child_dob <- as.Date(data_clean$child_dob)

#Let's make an age variable, calculated from the date of the survey and the date of birth
data_clean$child_age_years <- time_length(
  interval(data_clean$child_dob, data_clean$survey_date),
  unit = "years"
) |> floor()

```


```{r adding number of sources predictor}

english_sources<- data_clean %>%

french_sources<- data_clean %>%

  mutate(french_sources_n = rowSums(!is.na(across(-internal_id)))) %>%

first_min_sources<- data_clean %>%

  mutate(first_min_sources_n = rowSums(!is.na(across(-internal_id)))) %>%
  select(internal_id, first_min_sources_n)


second_min_sources<- data_clean %>%
  select(internal_id, caregiver_1_second_minority, caregiver_2_second_minority, older_siblings_second_minority, younger_siblings_second_minority, other_family_second_minority, child_friends_second_minority, teachers_second_minority) %>%
  mutate(second_min_sources_n = rowSums(!is.na(across(-internal_id)))) %>%
  select(internal_id, second_min_sources_n)

third_min_sources<- data_clean %>%
  select(internal_id, caregiver_1_third_minority, caregiver_2_third_minority, older_siblings_third_minority, younger_siblings_third_minority, other_family_third_minority, child_friends_third_minority, teachers_third_minority) %>%
  mutate(third_min_sources_n = rowSums(!is.na(across(-internal_id)))) %>%

all_language_sources<- english_sources %>%
  left_join(french_sources) %>%
  left_join(first_min_sources) %>%
  left_join(second_min_sources) %>%
  left_join(third_min_sources)


#Now let's join the sum of sources from each language into our dataset with predictors

clean_w_predictors <- data_clean %>%
  left_join(all_language_sources, by="internal_id")


#Also making a coarser caregiver sources predictor to match what we have in the first collection data

clean_w_predictors<- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    caregiver_sources_english =
      (caregiver_1_english = !is.na(caregiver_1_english)) + 
      (caregiver_2_english =  !is.na(caregiver_2_english)),

    caregiver_sources_french =
      (caregiver_1_french = !is.na(caregiver_1_french)) +
      (caregiver_2_french = !is.na(caregiver_2_french)),

    caregiver_sources_first_minority =
      (caregiver_1_first_minority = !is.na(caregiver_1_first_minority)) +
      (caregiver_2_first_minority = !is.na(caregiver_2_first_minority)),

    caregiver_sources_second_minority =
      (caregiver_1_second_minority = !is.na(caregiver_1_second_minority)) +
      (caregiver_2_second_minority = !is.na(caregiver_2_second_minority)),

    caregiver_sources_third_minority =
      (caregiver_1_third_minority = !is.na(caregiver_1_third_minority)) +
      (caregiver_2_third_minority = !is.na(caregiver_2_third_minority))
  )
```

```{r recode categories to numbers}

clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_active_use_category,
        child_french_active_use_category,
        child_first_min_active_use_category,
        child_second_min_active_use_category,
        child_third_min_active_use_category
      ),
      ~ recode(
        .x,
        "My child does not understand or speak this language" = 0,
        "My child understands this language, but rarely speaks in it" = 1,
        "My child speaks this language mainly when someone addresses them in that language" = 2,
        "My child speaks this language spontaneously" = 3
      )
    )
  )



clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        caregiver_1_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_1_third_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_english_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_french_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_first_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_second_min_proficiency,
        caregiver_2_third_min_proficiency,
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        .x == "They do not speak this language" ~ 0,
        .x == "Very poor" ~ 1,
        .x == "Poor" ~ 2,
        .x == "Acceptable" ~ 3,
        .x == "Good" ~ 4,
        .x == "Excellent" ~ 5,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      .names = "{.col}" 
    )
  )



clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        child_english_mixing,
        child_french_mixing,
        child_first_min_mixing,
        child_second_min_mixing,
        child_third_min_mixing
      ),
      ~ case_when(
        str_detect(.x, "^My child never uses other languages") ~ 1,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child mixes in a few words") ~ 2,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child speaks mainly in another language") ~ 3,
        str_detect(.x, "^My child never speaks") ~ NA_real_,
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      .names = "{.col}"
    )
  )
```

```{r making census bilingualism rate variable}

# ============================================================
# Create a Census Division-level multilingualism rate predictor
# ============================================================
#
# Goal:
# Estimate the proportion of people in each Quebec Census Division
# who report knowledge of multiple languages, using Statistics Canada
# 2021 Census data.
#
# The final variable, multilingual_rate, is:
#
#   multiple-language responses / total knowledge-of-language responses
#
# We then merge this regional rate into the survey dataset based on
# each participant's Census Division.


# 1. Retrieve Quebec Census Division names and geographic IDs
# -----------------------------------------------------------
#
# We first use cancensus to obtain the list of Quebec Census Divisions.
# We do not need a substantive Census variable at this stage, so
# v_CA21_1 is used only as a dummy vector to make the geography query.
#
# geo_uid is especially useful because it provides a stable geographic
# identifier that can later be matched to the GeoUID in the StatCan table.

qc_geo_cd <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),   # Quebec province code
  level = "CD",                # Census Division level
  vectors = "v_CA21_1"         # dummy vector; used only to retrieve geography
) %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  distinct(geo_uid, region_name)


# Clean the Census Division names so that they match the region names
# already used in the survey dataset.
#
# Some cancensus region names contain additional information in
# parentheses. We remove everything from the first opening parenthesis
# onward, then remove any trailing whitespace.

qc_geo_cd <- qc_geo_cd %>%
  mutate(
    census_subdivision = str_remove(region_name, "[(].*"),
    census_subdivision = str_remove(census_subdivision, "\\s+$")
  ) %>%
  select(-region_name)


# 2. Connect to Statistics Canada Table 98-10-0216-01
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# Table 98-10-0216-01 contains 2021 Census information on knowledge
# of languages, including separate columns for:
#
#   - total responses to knowledge of languages
#   - single-language responses
#   - multiple-language responses
#
# get_cansim_connection() is used instead of get_cansim() because
# this is a very large table. The connection allows us to filter the
# data before loading it fully into R memory.

#WARNING This line takes about 15 minutes to run unless you add a local cache space in your computer
#On October 21 the connection with the canada census server broke, before fixing, making a workarounf from the downloaded table instead of relying on the server
# knowledge_con <- get_cansim_connection(
#   "98-10-0216-01"
# )

# 2. Access the locally cached Statistics Canada table
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# On October 21, 2026, the cansim API began returning an
# invalid JSON response, preventing get_cansim_connection()
# from working.
#
# The previously downloaded census table remains available
# locally in Parquet format.
#
# We access it directly through arrow::open_dataset(),
# bypassing the API without downloading the table again.
#
# Like get_cansim_connection(), open_dataset() creates a
# lazy Arrow dataset, allowing filtering before collect().

knowledge_con <- arrow::open_dataset(
  "C:/Users/andre/cansim_cache/cansim_98100216_parquet_eng/98100216-eng.parquet"
)






# 3. Extract the relevant Quebec Census Division rows
# ---------------------------------------------------
#
# First, rename the very long StatCan column names to shorter,
# easier-to-read variable names.
#
# Then restrict the dataset to:
#
#   - all ages combined
#   - all genders combined
#   - Census estimates expressed as counts
#   - the overall "Total - Knowledge of languages" category
#   - Quebec Census Divisions only
#
# Quebec Census Division DGUIDs begin with "2021A000324":
#   2021 = Census year
#   24   = Quebec province code
#   CD   = Census Division geography
#
# Filtering is done while the data are still stored as an Arrow query,
# which avoids loading the full Statistics Canada table into memory.

qc_cd_multilingual_rate <- knowledge_con %>%
  rename(
    age = `Age (7)`,
    gender = `Gender (3)`,
    statistics = `Statistics (3)`,
    knowledge_of_languages = `Knowledge of languages (324)`,
    total_language_responses =
      `Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages (3):Total - Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages[1]`,
    multiple_language_responses =
      `Single and multiple responses of knowledge of languages (3):Multiple responses of knowledge of languages[3]`
  ) %>%

  filter(
    age == "Total - Age",
    gender == "Total - Gender",
    statistics == "Count",
    knowledge_of_languages == "Total - Knowledge of languages",

    # Keep Quebec Census Divisions only
    str_starts(DGUID, "2021A000324")
  ) %>%

  select(
    GEO,
    DGUID,
    GeoUID,
    total_language_responses,
    multiple_language_responses
  ) %>%

  # Only after filtering to the small subset we need do we load
  # the data into R as a regular tibble.
  collect()


# 4. Calculate the regional multilingualism rate
# ----------------------------------------------
#
# "Multiple responses of knowledge of languages" represents people
# reporting knowledge of more than one language.
#
# Dividing that count by the total number of knowledge-of-language
# responses gives the estimated proportion of the population in
# private households who know multiple languages within each
# Census Division.
#
# The result is stored as a proportion:
#   e.g., 0.42 = approximately 42% multilingual.

qc_cd_multilingual_rate <- qc_cd_multilingual_rate %>%
  mutate(
    multilingual_rate =
      multiple_language_responses / total_language_responses
  )


# 5. Match the StatCan multilingualism estimates to our Quebec
#    Census Division lookup table
# ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# GeoUID in the cansim table corresponds to geo_uid from cancensus.
#
# Joining by the geographic ID is preferable to joining by region name,
# because IDs are stable and avoid problems caused by accents,
# punctuation, spelling differences, or formatting.

# 5. Match StatCan multilingualism estimates to Census Divisions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# 5. Match StatCan multilingualism estimates to Census Divisions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cd_multilingual_rate <- qc_geo_cd %>%
  left_join(
    qc_cd_multilingual_rate %>%
      transmute(
        geo_uid = as.character(GeoUID),
        multilingual_rate
      ),
    by = "geo_uid"
  )
#sanity check after the october 21st issues

# Check how many Census Divisions received a multilingualism rate
cd_multilingual_rate %>%
  summarise(
    n_regions = n(),
    n_matched = sum(!is.na(multilingual_rate)),
    n_missing = sum(is.na(multilingual_rate)),
    min_rate = min(multilingual_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate = max(multilingual_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
  )



# 6. Merge the regional multilingualism rate into the survey data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each survey participant already has a census_subdivision variable.
# We therefore attach the Census Division-level multilingualism rate
# by matching participants to their Census Division.
#
# All participants living in the same Census Division receive the same
# regional multilingualism-rate value.

# 6. Harmonize geographic names and merge into survey data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

clean_w_predictors <- clean_w_predictors %>%

  # Remove columns from the previous join
  select(-any_of(c("multilingual_rate", "geo_uid"))) %>%

  # Standardize survey Census Division names
  mutate(
    census_subdivision = case_when(
      census_subdivision == "Les Îles-de-la-Madeleine" ~
        "Communauté maritime des Îles-de-la-Madeleine",

      census_subdivision == "Côte-de-Gaspé" ~
        "La Côte-de-Gaspé",

      TRUE ~ census_subdivision
    )
  ) %>%

  # Join using the harmonized names
  left_join(
    cd_multilingual_rate,
    by = "census_subdivision"
  )

```


```{r adding density of speaker by language}

# ============================================================
# Create regional speaker rates for languages heard by children
# using 2021 Census "Knowledge of languages" data
# ============================================================


# 1. Put children's languages into long format
# ---------------------------------------------

languages_heard <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  dplyr::select(
    internal_id,
    census_subdivision,
    child_english,
    child_french,
    child_first_minority,
    child_second_minority,
    child_third_minority,
    geo_uid
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = child_english:child_third_minority,
    names_to = "language_type",
    values_to = "language"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language = case_when(
      language == "Anglais" ~ "English",
      language == "Francais" ~ "French",
      language == "francais" ~ "French",
      language == "Berbère" ~ "Berber",
      language == "Portugais" ~ "Portuguese",
      language == "Allemand" ~ "German",
      language == "allemand" ~ "German",
      language == "italien" ~ "Italian",
      language == "Suisse-Allemand" ~ "German",
      language == "Espagnol" ~ "Spanish",
      language == "espagnol" ~ "Spanish",
      language == "hungarian" ~ "Hungarian",
      language == "Polonais" ~ "Polish",
      language == "polonais" ~ "Polish",
      language == "Spanish and German" ~ "German",
      language == "francaus et arabe" ~ "Arabic",
      language == "Bosnian (Serbian, Croatian)" ~ "Bosnian",
      language == "Grec" ~ "Greek",
      language == "Créole Reunionnais" ~ "Creole languages, n.i.e.",
      language == "Créole reunionnais" ~ "Creole languages, n.i.e.",
      language == "Créole réunionnais" ~ "Creole languages, n.i.e.",
      language == "créole haïtien" ~ "Haitian Creole",
       language == "le lingala" ~ "Lingala",
      language == "Italien" ~ "Italian",
      language == "Lsq" ~ "QSL",
      language == "LSQ" ~ "QSL",
      language == "Arménien" ~ "Armenian",
      language == "Malgache" ~ "Malagasy",
      language == "Cri" ~ "Cree",
      language == "Russe" ~ "Russian",
      language == "Arabe" ~ "Arabic",
language %in% c("Mooré", "Moore", "Banen") ~
  "Niger-Congo languages, n.i.e.",
      language == "Non"~ NA,
      TRUE ~ language
    )
  )


# Create a list of the unique languages represented in the survey.
# This is useful for checking whether our survey labels match the
# Statistics Canada language labels.

survey_languages <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  arrange(language)



# ============================================================
# Retrieve 2021 Census "Knowledge of languages" vectors
# ============================================================

ca21_vectors <- list_census_vectors("CA21")


# v_CA21_3229 is the parent vector for:
# "Knowledge of languages for the population in private households"
#
# This is based on the 2021 Census 25% sample data and contains
# both official and non-official languages.

knowledge_language_children <- child_census_vectors(
  "v_CA21_3229",
  leaves_only = TRUE
)


# Keep only the individual language vectors.
#
# Using leaves_only = TRUE removes broad aggregate categories such as
# "Official languages", "Non-official languages", "Indigenous languages",
# etc., leaving the most specific language categories available.

language_lookup <- knowledge_language_children %>%
  select(
    vector,
    census_language = label
  )



#to avoid breaking the r memory by querying too many languages at once, I will break up the query into batches

language_vectors <- language_lookup$vector

# ============================================================
# Download the language counts for Quebec Census Divisions
# ============================================================
#
# The Census contains many language vectors, so the vectors are split
# into batches of 50 to avoid making a very large query at once.

language_vectors <- language_lookup$vector

vector_batches <- split(
  language_vectors,
  ceiling(seq_along(language_vectors) / 50)
)


language_batches <- lapply(
  vector_batches,
  function(x) {
    get_census(
      dataset = "CA21",
      regions = list(PR = "24"),
      level = "CD",
      vectors = x,
      labels = "short"
    )
  }
)

# Start with the first batch.

qc_cd_languages_wide <- language_batches[[1]]


# Add the remaining batches by matching Census Divisions on GeoUID.

if (length(language_batches) > 1) {

  for (i in 2:length(language_batches)) {

    new_cols <- setdiff(
      names(language_batches[[i]]),
      names(qc_cd_languages_wide)
    )

    qc_cd_languages_wide <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
      left_join(
        language_batches[[i]] %>%
          select(GeoUID, all_of(new_cols)),
        by = "GeoUID"
      )
  }
}


census_language_cd <- qc_cd_languages_wide %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("v_CA21_"),
    names_to = "vector",
    values_to = "language_knowledge_n"
  )

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    language_lookup,
    by = "vector"
  )


# ============================================================
# Retrieve denominator for language knowledge rates
# ============================================================
#
# v_CA21_3229 represents the population in private households
# covered by the Census "Knowledge of languages" measure.
#
# Using this as the denominator ensures that the language-specific
# counts and the population denominator come from the same Census
# concept and statistical universe.

cd_population_knowledge <- get_census(
  dataset = "CA21",
  regions = list(PR = "24"),
  level = "CD",
  vectors = "v_CA21_3229",
  labels = "short"
)


cd_population_knowledge <- cd_population_knowledge %>%
  select(
    GeoUID,
    knowledge_language_population = v_CA21_3229
  )



# ============================================================
# Calculate regional prevalence of knowledge of each language
# ============================================================

census_language_cd <- census_language_cd %>%
  left_join(
    cd_population_knowledge,
    by = "GeoUID"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language_knowledge_rate =
      language_knowledge_n / knowledge_language_population,

    language_knowledge_percent =
      language_knowledge_rate * 100
  )




#Check language matches

language_crosswalk <- languages_heard %>%
  distinct(language) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language)) %>%
  rename(survey_language = language) %>%
  mutate(
    census_language = case_when(
      survey_language == "Berber" ~ "Berber languages, n.i.e.",
      survey_language == "Persian" ~ "Persian (Farsi), n.o.s.",
      survey_language == "Punjabi" ~ "Punjabi (Panjabi)",
      survey_language == "Malagasy" ~ "Malagasy, n.o.s.",
      survey_language == "QSL" ~ "Quebec Sign Language",
      survey_language == "Cree" ~ "Cree, n.o.s.",
      TRUE ~ survey_language
    ),

    exact_match =
      census_language %in% language_lookup$census_language
  )


finding_mismatches<- language_crosswalk %>%
  filter(!exact_match)



#final joins
census_lookup_final <- language_crosswalk %>%
  select(
    survey_language,
    census_language
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    census_language_cd,
    by = "census_language"
  )


data_clean_long <- languages_heard %>%
  left_join(
    census_lookup_final %>%
      select(
        survey_language,
        GeoUID,
        language_knowledge_n,
        knowledge_language_population,
        language_knowledge_rate,
        language_knowledge_percent
      ),
    by = c(
      "language" = "survey_language",
      "geo_uid" = "GeoUID"
    )
  )
```

```{r statistical analyses language specific}
    minority_book_resources_third = book_resources_third_minority,

    # Book reading
    minority_book_reading_first = caregiver_first_min_book_reading,
    minority_book_reading_second = caregiver_second_min_book_reading,
    minority_book_reading_third = caregiver_third_min_book_reading,

    # Active use
    minority_active_use_first = child_first_min_active_use_category,
    minority_active_use_second = child_second_min_active_use_category,
    minority_active_use_third = child_third_min_active_use_category,

    # Interlocutor matching

  # Turn first/second/third into rows
```

```{r visualizations}
extract_outcome_cor <- function(cor_matrix, outcome_var, language_group, outcome_label) {
  
  vals <- cor_matrix[outcome_var, , drop = TRUE]
  
  tibble(
    predictor = names(vals),
    correlation = as.numeric(vals),
    language_group = language_group,
    outcome = outcome_label
  )
}

    french_correlation,
    "child_french_active_use_category",
```

```{r hirarchical linear mixed effects models}
# ============================================================
# 1. Build base model for both outcomes

#a. Standardize predictors


model_data_long <- model_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(
        overall_exposure,
        child_age_years,
        speaker_rate,
        book_resources,
        book_reading,
        number_sources,
        # status_attitudes,
        # solidarity_attitudes,
        # cognition_attitudes,
        # exposure_fluency_concern,
        # concern_cognitive_difficulties,
        # concern_school_difficulties
      ),
      ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)),
      .names = "{.col}_z"
    )
  )

#b. creating match databases so that the models are comparable 

all_predictors <- c(
  "overall_exposure_z",
  "child_age_years_z",
  "speaker_rate_z",
  "book_resources_z",
  "book_reading_z",
  "number_sources_z"
)


# Dataset for active use
active_data <- model_data_long %>%
  drop_na(
    internal_id,
    active_use,
    all_of(all_predictors)
  )

# Dataset for interlocutor matching
matching_data <- model_data_long %>%
  drop_na(
    internal_id,
    interlocutor_matching,
    all_of(all_predictors)
  )




#c. build base models
active_base <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

performance(active_base)

matching_base <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

performance(matching_base)

# ============================================================
# 2. add societal layer predictors and compare to base model

#a. Build the models
active_societal <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

summary(active_societal)
#exposure and age are significant, societal factors are not

performance(active_societal)

matching_societal <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
        speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

summary(matching_societal)
#exposure, age and speaker rate is marginal

#b. Do ANOVAS between base and societal level layers

anova(active_base, active_societal) #no difference, better fit with base model

anova(matching_base, matching_societal) #marginal difference, slightly better fit for the societal in AIC but not BIC

# ============================================================
# 2. build family layer predictor models and compare to base model

active_family <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(active_family)

matching_family <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
        book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)



# ============================================================
# 3. add societal layer predictors and compare to base and single layer models

#a. Build the models
active_both_layers <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)
summary(active_family)

matching_both_layers <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
        speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
        book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_data,
  REML = FALSE,
  na.action = na.omit
)

summary(matching_family)

#anovas between base, societal, and family models

anova(active_base, active_societal, active_family) #family significantly better than societal
anova(matching_base, matching_societal, matching_family) #family marginally better than societal
anova(matching_base, matching_family) #family significantly better than base
anova(matching_family, matching_both_layers)

# Extract random-intercept SD
get_intercept_sd <- function(model) {
  as.numeric(
    attr(VarCorr(model)$internal_id, "stddev")[1]
  )
}

# Extract residual SD
get_residual_sd <- function(model) {
  sigma(model)
}

# Create rows for the table
sd_rows <- data.frame(
  term = c(
    "SD (Random intercept: Child)",
    "SD (Residuals)"
  ),
  Societal = c(
    get_intercept_sd(active_societal),
    get_residual_sd(active_societal)
  ),
  Family = c(
    get_intercept_sd(active_family),
    get_residual_sd(active_family)
  ),
  `Both layers` = c(
    get_intercept_sd(active_both_layers),
    get_residual_sd(active_both_layers)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Format to 3 decimal places
sd_rows[-1] <- lapply(
  sd_rows[-1],
  function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
)

# Place these rows after the coefficients
attr(sd_rows, "position") <- "gof_start"



# Generate publication-ready table

table_active <- modelsummary(
  models_active,
  coef_map = coef_names,
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = c(
    "+" = 0.10,
    "*" = 0.05,
    "**" = 0.01,
    "***" = 0.001
  ),
  fmt = 3,
  gof_map = gof_active,
  add_rows = sd_rows,
  output = "flextable"
)

table_active <- table_active |>
  theme_booktabs() |>
  autofit() |>
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
  align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all")

table_active



save_as_docx(
  "Table 1. Linear mixed-effects models predicting active language use" =
    table_active,
  path = "active_use_models.docx"
)

# ============================================================
#Let's make a publication ready table of the matching results


# Models in the desired order
models_matching <- list(
  "Societal" = matching_societal,
  "Family" = matching_family,
  "Both layers" = matching_both_layers
)

# Rename predictors for publication
coef_names <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  "overall_exposure_z" = "Overall language exposure",
  "child_age_years_z" = "Child age",
  "speaker_rate_z" = "Speaker rate",
  "book_resources_z" = "Book resources",
  "book_reading_z" = "Book reading",
  "number_sources_z" = "Number of language sources"
)



gof_matching <- data.frame(
  raw = c(
    "nobs",
    "r2.marginal",
    "r2.conditional",
    "aic",
    "bic",
    "rmse"
  ),
  clean = c(
    "Observations",
    "Marginal R²",
    "Conditional R²",
    "AIC",
    "BIC",
    "RMSE"
  ),
  fmt = c(0, 3, 3, 1, 1, 3)
)


# Extract random-intercept SD
get_intercept_sd <- function(model) {
  as.numeric(
    attr(VarCorr(model)$internal_id, "stddev")[1]
  )
}

# Extract residual SD
get_residual_sd <- function(model) {
  sigma(model)
}

# Create rows for the table
sd_rows <- data.frame(
  term = c(
    "SD (Random intercept: Child)",
    "SD (Residuals)"
  ),
  Societal = c(
    get_intercept_sd(matching_societal),
    get_residual_sd(matching_societal)
  ),
  Family = c(
    get_intercept_sd(matching_family),
    get_residual_sd(matching_family)
  ),
  `Both layers` = c(
    get_intercept_sd(matching_both_layers),
    get_residual_sd(matching_both_layers)
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Format to 3 decimal places
sd_rows[-1] <- lapply(
  sd_rows[-1],
  function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
)

# Place these rows after the coefficients
attr(sd_rows, "position") <- "gof_start"



# Generate publication-ready table

table_matching <- modelsummary(
  models_matching,
  coef_map = coef_names,
  estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
  statistic = "({std.error})",
  stars = c(
    "+" = 0.10,
    "*" = 0.05,
    "**" = 0.01,
    "***" = 0.001
  ),
  fmt = 3,
  gof_map = gof_matching,
  add_rows = sd_rows,
  output = "flextable"
)

table_matching <- table_matching |>
  theme_booktabs() |>
  autofit() |>
  fontsize(size = 10, part = "all") |>
  align(align = "center", part = "all") |>
  align(j = 1, align = "left", part = "all")

table_matching

library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare plotting data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

interaction_data <- model_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language_type))

table(interaction_data$language_type)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Function to create interaction plots
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot_interaction <- function(data, predictor, outcome,
                             x_label, y_label) {

  ggplot(
    data,
    aes(
      x = .data[[predictor]],
      y = .data[[outcome]],
      color = language_type,
      fill = language_type
    )
  ) +
    geom_point(
      alpha = 0.25,
      size = 1.8,
      position = position_jitter(
        width = 0.05,
        height = 0
      )
    ) +
    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = TRUE,
      linewidth = 1.2,
      alpha = 0.15
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Community" = "#8DAEE1",
        "Heritage" = "#B0DA87"
      )
    ) +
    labs(
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label,
      color = "Language type",
      fill = "Language type"
    ) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 13) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define predictors to visualize
# ------------------------------------------------------------

predictors <- tibble(
  predictor = c(
    "overall_exposure_z",
    "speaker_rate_z",
    "book_resources_z",
    "book_reading_z",
    "number_sources_z"
  ),
  label = c(
    "Overall language exposure (z)",
    "Speaker rate (z)",
    "Access to books (z)",
    "Book reading (z)",
    "Number of language sources (z)"
  ),
  title = c(
    "Exposure",
    "Speaker rate",
    "Book resources",
    "Reading",
    "Sources"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Create plots for both outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

active_plots <- purrr::map2(
  predictors$predictor,
  predictors$label,
  ~ plot_interaction(
    interaction_data,
    .x,
    "active_use",
    .y,
    "Active language use"
  )
)

matching_plots <- purrr::map2(
  predictors$predictor,
  predictors$label,
  ~ plot_interaction(
    interaction_data,
    .x,
    "interlocutor_matching",
    .y,
    "Interlocutor matching (%)"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Apply formatting
# ------------------------------------------------------------

larger_theme <- theme(
  plot.title = element_text(
    size = 15,
    face = "bold",
    margin = margin(b = 8)
  ),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
  plot.margin = margin(8, 8, 8, 8)
)

# Arrange plots row by row:
# Active use (left), Matching (right)

all_plots <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(predictors))) {

  active_plots[[i]] <- active_plots[[i]] +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        LETTERS[2 * i - 1], ". ",
        predictors$title[i],
        " × Language type"
      )
    ) +
    larger_theme

  matching_plots[[i]] <- matching_plots[[i]] +
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        LETTERS[2 * i], ". ",
        predictors$title[i],
        " × Language type"
      )
    ) +
    larger_theme

  all_plots <- append(
    all_plots,
    list(active_plots[[i]], matching_plots[[i]])
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Combine into 2 columns x 5 rows
# ------------------------------------------------------------

interaction_figure <- wrap_plots(
  all_plots,
  ncol = 2,
  guides = "collect"
) &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

interaction_figure

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Save high-resolution figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  "exploratory_language_interactions_full.png",
  interaction_figure,
  width = 10,
  height = 20,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "white"
)

# ============================================================
# 5. EXPLORATORY INTERACTION MODELS
# Full both-layers approach
# ============================================================

library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Prepare data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

interaction_data <- model_data_long %>%
  mutate(
    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(language_type))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. ACTIVE LANGUAGE USE
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Complete cases for all predictors

active_int_data <- interaction_data %>%
  drop_na(
    active_use,
    overall_exposure_z,
    child_age_years_z,
    speaker_rate_z,
    book_resources_z,
    book_reading_z,
    number_sources_z,
    language_type,
    internal_id
  )

# Main-effects model: both layers

active_main <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    language_type +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_int_data,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Full interaction model:
# All environmental predictors interact with language type

active_interaction <- lmer(
  active_use ~
    overall_exposure_z * language_type +
    speaker_rate_z * language_type +
    book_resources_z * language_type +
    book_reading_z * language_type +
    number_sources_z * language_type +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = active_int_data,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Compare models
anova(active_main, active_interaction)

# Inspect coefficients
summary(active_interaction)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. INTERLOCUTOR MATCHING
# ------------------------------------------------------------

matching_int_data <- interaction_data %>%
  drop_na(
    interlocutor_matching,
    overall_exposure_z,
    child_age_years_z,
    speaker_rate_z,
    book_resources_z,
    book_reading_z,
    number_sources_z,
    language_type,
    internal_id
  )

# Main-effects model: both layers

matching_main <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z +
    child_age_years_z +
    speaker_rate_z +
    book_resources_z +
    book_reading_z +
    number_sources_z +
    language_type +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_int_data,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Full interaction model

matching_interaction <- lmer(
  interlocutor_matching ~
    overall_exposure_z * language_type +
    speaker_rate_z * language_type +
    book_resources_z * language_type +
    book_reading_z * language_type +
    number_sources_z * language_type +
    child_age_years_z +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = matching_int_data,
  REML = FALSE
)

# Compare models
anova(matching_main, matching_interaction)

# Inspect coefficients
summary(matching_interaction)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Check observations and model diagnostics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sapply(
  list(
    active_main = active_main,
    active_interaction = active_interaction,
    matching_main = matching_main,
    matching_interaction = matching_interaction
  ),
  nobs
)

# Check singular fits
sapply(
  list(
    active_main = active_main,
    active_interaction = active_interaction,
    matching_main = matching_main,
    matching_interaction = matching_interaction
  ),
  lme4::isSingular
)




library(broom.mixed)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

interaction_results <- bind_rows(
  broom.mixed::tidy(
    active_interaction,
    effects = "fixed"
  ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = "Active language use"),

  broom.mixed::tidy(
    matching_interaction,
    effects = "fixed"
  ) %>%
    mutate(outcome = "Interlocutor matching")
) %>%
  filter(grepl(":", term)) %>%
  select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value),
      ~ round(.x, 3)
    )
  )

interaction_results
```

```{r statistical analyses language agnostic}
  select(internal_id, child_french_active_use_category, child_english_active_use_category, child_first_min_active_use_category, child_second_min_active_use_category, child_third_min_active_use_category, child_french_interlocutor_matching, child_english_interlocutor_matching, child_first_min_interlocutor_matching, child_second_min_interlocutor_matching, child_third_min_interlocutor_matching)


#making a binary measure of degree of activeness where all the languages must be at or above a score of 2 to receive 1, otherwise they receive 0.

lang_agnostic_outcomes <- lang_agnostic_outcomes %>%
  mutate(
    degree_of_activeness_combined = as.integer(
      if_all(
        ends_with("_active_use_category"),
        ~ is.na(.x) | .x >= 2
      )
    )
  ) %>%
#making a binary measure of language matching where all the languages must be at or above a score of 50% to receive 1, otherwise they receive 0.
  mutate(
    language_matching_combined = as.integer(
      if_all(
        ends_with("_interlocutor_matching"),
        ~ is.na(.x) | .x >= 50
      )
    )
  ) 

lang_agnostic_outcomes <- lang_agnostic_outcomes %>%
  select(internal_id, language_matching_combined, degree_of_activeness_combined)

  for_agnostic_models <- lang_agnostic_predictors %>%
   left_join(lang_agnostic_outcomes, by="internal_id")
```

```{r logistic models}
    worry_school_difficulties_z,
  data = logistic_complete,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

#==========================================
#fit logistic models for language matching



# Societal model
matching_societal_log <- glm(
  language_matching_combined ~
    child_age_years_z +
    multilingual_rate_z,
  data = logistic_complete,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# Family model
matching_family_log <- glm(
  language_matching_combined ~
    child_age_years_z +
    beleifs_ahead_in_life_z +
    beleifs_belonging_z +
    beliefs_cognitive_benefits_z +
    worry_master_languages_z +
    worry_cognitive_difficulties_z +
    worry_school_difficulties_z,
  data = logistic_complete,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)

# Both layers
matching_both_log <- glm(
  language_matching_combined ~
    child_age_years_z +
    multilingual_rate_z +
    beleifs_ahead_in_life_z +
    beleifs_belonging_z +
    beliefs_cognitive_benefits_z +
    worry_master_languages_z +
    worry_cognitive_difficulties_z +
    worry_school_difficulties_z,
  data = logistic_complete,
  family = binomial(link = "logit")
)


#=======================================================
#Create publication ready tables


coef_names_log <- c(
  "(Intercept)" = "Intercept",
  "child_age_years_z" = "Child age",
  "multilingual_rate_z" = "Multilingualism rate",
  "beleifs_ahead_in_life_z" = "Beliefs: Future opportunities",
  "beleifs_belonging_z" = "Beliefs: Belonging",
  "beliefs_cognitive_benefits_z" = "Beliefs: Cognitive benefits",
  "worry_master_languages_z" = "Concern: Language mastery",
  "worry_cognitive_difficulties_z" = "Concern: Cognitive difficulties",
  "worry_school_difficulties_z" = "Concern: School difficulties"
)

# McFadden's pseudo-R²
mcfadden_r2 <- function(model) {
  1 - as.numeric(
    logLik(model) / logLik(update(model, . ~ 1))
  )
}

# Define additional model statistics
glance_custom.glm <- function(x, ...) {
  data.frame(
    mcfadden = mcfadden_r2(x)
  )
}

# Goodness-of-fit statistics
gof_log <- data.frame(
  raw = c(
    "nobs",
    "mcfadden",
    "aic",
    "bic"
  ),
  clean = c(
    "Observations",
    "McFadden's pseudo-R²",
    "AIC",
    "BIC"
  ),
  fmt = c(0, 3, 1, 1)
)

  models_active_log,

exponentiate = FALSE,
estimate = "{estimate}{stars}",
statistic = "({std.error})",
  conf_level = 0.95,
  stars = c(
    "+" = 0.10,
    "*" = 0.05,
    "**" = 0.01,
    "***" = 0.001
  ),
  fmt = 3,
  gof_map = gof_log,

)

# Function to extract likelihood-ratio comparisons
extract_lr <- function(model_small, model_large,
                       outcome, comparison) {

  result <- anova(
    model_small,
    model_large,
    test = "Chisq"
  )

  tibble(
    Outcome = outcome,
    Comparison = comparison,
    Chi_square = result$Deviance[2],
    df = result$Df[2],
    p = result$`Pr(>Chi)`[2]
  )
}

anova_log_table <- bind_rows(
  extract_lr(
    active_societal_log,
    active_both_log,
    "Degree of activeness",
    "Societal vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    active_family_log,
    active_both_log,
    "Degree of activeness",
    "Family vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    matching_societal_log,
    matching_both_log,
    "Language matching",
    "Societal vs. both"
  ),
  extract_lr(
    matching_family_log,
    matching_both_log,
    "Language matching",
    "Family vs. both"
  )
) %>%
  mutate(
    Chi_square = round(Chi_square, 2),
    p = ifelse(
      p < .001,
      "< .001",
      sprintf("%.3f", p)
    )
  )

anova_log_flex <- flextable(anova_log_table) |>
  set_header_labels(
    Chi_square = "χ²",
    df = "df",
    p = "p"
  ) |>
  theme_booktabs() |>
  autofit()

anova_log_flex
```

```{r methods descriptives}
# 1. IDENTIFY EACH CHILD'S LANGUAGE COMBINATION


language_composition <- model_data_long %>%
  
  # One row per child-language
  distinct(internal_id, language, language_type) %>%
  
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  
  summarise(
    n_languages = n_distinct(language),
    
    n_english = sum(language_type == "English"),
    n_french = sum(language_type == "French"),
    n_minority = sum(language_type == "Minority"),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  
  # Broad number-of-languages category
  mutate(
    multilingual_group = case_when(
      n_languages == 1 ~ "Monolingual",
      n_languages == 2 ~ "Bilingual",
      n_languages == 3 ~ "Trilingual",
      n_languages >= 4 ~ "4+ languages"
    ),
    
    # Composition within each category
    language_combination = case_when(
      
      # -----------------------
      # Monolingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 1 & n_english == 1 ~ "English",
      n_languages == 1 & n_french == 1 ~ "French",
      n_languages == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~ "Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # Bilingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_english == 1 & n_french == 1 ~
        "English + French",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_english == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~
        "English + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_french == 1 & n_minority == 1 ~
        "French + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 2 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "Minority + Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # Trilingual
      # -----------------------
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_english == 1 &
        n_french == 1 &
        n_minority == 1 ~
        "English + French + Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_english == 1 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "English + 2 Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_french == 1 &
        n_minority == 2 ~
        "French + 2 Minority",
      
      n_languages == 3 &
        n_minority == 3 ~
        "3 Minority",
      
      
      # -----------------------
      # 4+
      # -----------------------
      n_languages >= 4 ~ "4+ languages",
      
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    )
  )



language_composition %>%
  count(
    multilingual_group,
    language_combination
  )


# ============================================================
# 2. CREATE STACKED-BAR DATA
# ============================================================

language_composition_summary <- language_composition %>%
```

```{r predictors tables methods}
library(tidyverse)

# Replace this if your child-level analysis dataset
# has a different name.
child_data <- logistic_data %>%

# Language-level observations

  mutate(
    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")
    )
  )

# Dictionary of predictors
# Edit names if they differ from your current dataset.

predictor_dictionary <- tribble(
  ~variable, ~label, ~analyses_level, ~layer,

  "child_age_years", "Child age (years)",
  "Both", "Child characteristics",

  "multilingual_rate", "Multilingualism rate",
  "Language agnostic", "Societal environment",

  "speaker_rate", "By-language speaker rate",
  "Language specific", "Societal environment",

  "book_resources", "Access to books",
  "Language specific", "Family environment",

  "overall_exposure", "Overall language exposure",
  "Language specific", "Family environment",

  "book_reading", "Book reading",
  "Language specific", "Family environment",

  "number_sources", "Number of language sources",
  "Language specific", "Family environment",

  "beleifs_ahead_in_life", "Status attitudes",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment",

  "beleifs_belonging", "Solidarity attitudes",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment",

  "beliefs_cognitive_benefits", "Cognition attitudes",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment",

  "worry_master_languages", "Exposure-fluency concern",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment",

  "worry_cognitive_difficulties",
  "Cognitive difficulties concern",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment",

  "worry_school_difficulties",
  "School difficulties concern",
  "Language agnostic", "Family environment"
)

# Check which variables are missing
predictor_dictionary %>%
  mutate(
    available = map2_lgl(variable, analyses_level, function(v, lvl) {
      v %in% names(
        if (lvl == "Child") child_data else language_data
      )
    })
  ) %>%
  filter(!available)



summarise_predictor <- function(data, variable) {

  x <- data[[variable]]

  if (!is.numeric(x)) {
    stop("Variable is not numeric: ", variable)
  }

  x <- x[is.finite(x)]

  tibble(
    N = length(x),
    Mean = if (length(x)) mean(x) else NA_real_,
    SD = if (length(x) > 1) sd(x) else NA_real_,
    Median = if (length(x)) median(x) else NA_real_,
    Minimum = if (length(x)) min(x) else NA_real_,
    Maximum = if (length(x)) max(x) else NA_real_
  )
}


# ============================================================
# Create descriptive statistics for all predictors
# using the updated predictor dictionary
# ============================================================

make_predictor_summary <- function(
    dictionary,
    child_data,
    language_data
) {

  results <- vector("list", nrow(dictionary))

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(dictionary))) {

    # Extract information from dictionary
    v <- dictionary$variable[i]
    analysis <- dictionary$analyses_level[i]

    # Select dataset based on analysis level
    if (analysis %in% c("Both", "Language agnostic")) {

      dat <- child_data

    } else if (analysis == "Language specific") {

      dat <- language_data

    } else {

      stop(
        "Unknown analyses_level for variable ",
        v, ": ", analysis
      )
    }

    # Check that variable exists in selected dataset
    if (!v %in% names(dat)) {
      stop(
        "Variable '", v,
        "' not found in dataset for ",
        analysis
      )
    }

    # Calculate descriptive statistics
    results[[i]] <- dplyr::bind_cols(
      dictionary[i, ],
      summarise_predictor(dat, v)
    )
  }

  # Combine all predictor summaries
  dplyr::bind_rows(results)
}

# ============================================================
# Generate overall descriptive statistics
# ============================================================

overall_summary <- make_predictor_summary(
  dictionary = predictor_dictionary,
  child_data = child_data,
  language_data = language_data
)

overall_summary



format_predictor_table <- function(summary_data) {

  summary_data %>%
    mutate(
      `M (SD)` = if_else(
        is.na(SD),
        sprintf("%.2f (—)", Mean),
        sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", Mean, SD)
      ),
      Median = sprintf("%.2f", Median),
      Range = sprintf("%.2f–%.2f", Minimum, Maximum)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Layer = layer,
      Predictor = label,
      `Analysis level` = analyses_level,
      N,
      `M (SD)`,
      Median,
      Range
    )
}

# Prepare long-format distributions using the

# ============================================================
# Prepare predictor distributions for supplementary figure
# ============================================================

distribution_list <- lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(predictor_dictionary)),
  function(i) {

    # Extract variable and analysis level
    v <- predictor_dictionary$variable[i]
    analysis <- predictor_dictionary$analyses_level[i]

    # Select the appropriate dataset
    if (analysis %in% c("Both", "Language agnostic")) {

      dat <- child_data

    } else if (analysis == "Language specific") {

      dat <- language_data

    } else {

      stop(
        "Unknown analyses_level for variable ",
        v, ": ", analysis
      )
    }

    # Check that variable exists
    if (!v %in% names(dat)) {
      stop("Variable not found: ", v)
    }

    # Create long-format distribution data
tibble(
  Variable = predictor_dictionary$label[i],
  Analysis_level = analysis,
  Layer = predictor_dictionary$layer[i],
  Value = as.numeric(dat[[v]])
)
  }
)

# Combine distributions into one dataframe
predictor_distributions <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  distribution_list
) %>%
  filter(is.finite(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(
      Variable,
      levels = unique(predictor_dictionary$label)
    )
  )

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ============================================================
# STEP 1: Identify each child's language group
# ============================================================

language_groups <- clean_w_predictors %>%
  select(
    internal_id,
    child_english,
    child_french,
    child_first_minority,
    child_second_minority,
    child_third_minority
  ) %>%
  distinct(internal_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -internal_id,
    names_to = "language_source",
    values_to = "language"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language = str_squish(as.character(language)),
    language = case_when(
      str_to_lower(language) %in%
        c("english", "anglais") ~ "English",

      str_to_lower(language) %in%
        c("french", "français", "francais") ~ "French",

      TRUE ~ language
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(language),
    language != ""
  ) %>%
  distinct(internal_id, language) %>%
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_languages = n(),
    has_french = any(language == "French"),
    has_english = any(language == "English"),
    n_heritage = sum(
      !language %in% c("French", "English")
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language_group = case_when(
      n_languages >= 3 ~ "Trilinguals+",

      n_languages == 2 &
        has_french & has_english ~
        "Community bilinguals",

      n_languages == 2 &
        n_heritage == 1 ~
        "Community–Heritage bilinguals",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    language_group = factor(
      language_group,
      levels = c(
        "Community bilinguals",
        "Community–Heritage bilinguals",
        "Trilinguals+"
      )
    )
  )

# Check group sizes
language_groups %>%
  count(language_group)

# STEP 2: Join language groups to binary outcome

#Let's do a chi-square test of independence to see if thecategories of children who score 1 in the binary score are distributed the same way they are in our sample 



# Create contingency table
activeness_table <- table(
  binary_plot_data$language_group,
  binary_plot_data$degree_of_activeness_combined
)

activeness_table

# Pearson chi-square test
chi_result <- chisq.test(
  activeness_table,
  correct = FALSE
)

chi_result

# Check expected frequencies
chi_result$expected

# Standardized Pearson residuals
chi_result$stdres

# Cramer's V
cramers_v <- sqrt(
  unname(chi_result$statistic) /
    (sum(activeness_table) *
       min(dim(activeness_table) - 1))
)

cramers_v



# Summarize binary outcome by language group
pairwise_data <- binary_plot_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(language_group),
    !is.na(degree_of_activeness_combined)
  ) %>%
  group_by(language_group) %>%
  summarise(
    n_score_1 = sum(degree_of_activeness_combined == 1),
    N = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Pairwise comparisons of proportions
pairwise_result <- pairwise.prop.test(
  x = pairwise_data$n_score_1,
  n = pairwise_data$N,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
)

pairwise_result


#Let's then also make a sensitivity analyses that does not punish trilingual children making them harder to achieve the score of 1 because they have to surpass the threshold for more languages

# ============================================================
# STEP 1: Calculate proportion of active languages per child
# ============================================================

child_activeness <- model_data_long %>%
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_languages = n(),
    n_valid = sum(!is.na(active_use)),

    n_active = sum(
      active_use >= 2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    proportion_active = if_else(
      n_valid > 0,
      n_active / n_valid,
      NA_real_
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Join language group classifications
sensitivity_data <- child_activeness %>%
  left_join(
    language_groups %>%
      select(internal_id, language_group),
    by = "internal_id"
  )

# Check results
sensitivity_data %>%
  group_by(language_group) %>%
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    Mean_proportion = mean(
      proportion_active,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    SD = sd(
      proportion_active,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    Median = median(
      proportion_active,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )



# ============================================================
# STEP 2: Visualize proportions across language groups
# ============================================================

sensitivity_plot <- sensitivity_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(language_group),
    !is.na(proportion_active)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = language_group,
      y = proportion_active,
      fill = language_group
    )
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    width = 0.15,
    height = 0,
    alpha = 0.35,
    size = 2,
    shape = 21
  ) +
  stat_summary(
    fun = mean,
    geom = "point",
    shape = 23,
    size = 4,
    fill = "white",
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Community bilinguals" = "#8DAEE1",
      "Community–Heritage bilinguals" = "#B0DA87",
      "Trilinguals+" = "#FAE0BD"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    limits = c(0, 1)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Proportion of languages meeting activeness criterion",
    title = "Sensitivity analysis: Proportion of active languages"
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 15,
      hjust = 1
    )
  )

sensitivity_plot



# ============================================================
# STEP 3: Kruskal-Wallis test
# ============================================================

sensitivity_complete <- sensitivity_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(language_group),
    !is.na(proportion_active)
  )

kruskal_result <- kruskal.test(
  proportion_active ~ language_group,
  data = sensitivity_complete
)

kruskal_result


pairwise.wilcox.test(
  x = sensitivity_complete$proportion_active,
  g = sensitivity_complete$language_group,
  p.adjust.method = "holm",
  exact = FALSE
)


# ============================================================
# STEP 4: Exploratory binomial regression
# ============================================================

binomial_model <- glm(
  cbind(
    n_active,
    n_valid - n_active
  ) ~ language_group,
  data = sensitivity_data %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(language_group),
      n_valid > 0
    ),
  family = binomial
)

summary(binomial_model)

# Omnibus test of language group
drop1(
  binomial_model,
  test = "Chisq"
)


#Sensitivity analyses show no differences between groups, meaning that the stringent binary outcome causes the group differences, that is, if children did not have to speak more than two languages, the groups would be comparable, but because some do have to... those children tend to get less classified as 'active users' In other words. It is harder to be an active user when you have to speak three languages.

# ============================================================

inactive_language_data <- model_data_long %>%
  left_join(

  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Language-level binary classification

      is.na(active_use) ~ NA_integer_,
      active_use >= 2 ~ 1L,
      active_use < 2 ~ 0L
    ),

    # Community vs heritage classification
    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")

  ) %>%
  group_by(internal_id) %>%
  mutate(
    n_valid = sum(!is.na(is_active)),
    n_inactive = sum(is_active == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    has_inactive_language = n_inactive > 0
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    has_inactive_language,
    !is.na(is_active),
    !is.na(language_group),
    !is.na(language_type)
  )

  "Figure_inactive_languages_three_groups.pdf",
  final_inactive_figure,
  width = 11,

# Mac nemar tests for the community language group and the comunity heritage groups


community_paired <- inactive_language_data %>%
  filter(
    language_group == "Community bilinguals"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    language = case_when(
      str_to_lower(str_squish(as.character(language))) %in%
        c("english", "anglais") ~ "English",
      str_to_lower(str_squish(as.character(language))) %in%
        c("french", "français", "francais") ~ "French",
      TRUE ~ as.character(language)
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(language %in% c("French", "English")) %>%
  select(internal_id, language, is_active) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = language,
    values_from = is_active
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(French), !is.na(English))

# French below threshold, English active
b <- sum(
  community_paired$French == 0 &
  community_paired$English == 1
)

# English below threshold, French active
c <- sum(
  community_paired$French == 1 &
  community_paired$English == 0
)

# Exact paired test
if (b + c > 0) {
  binom.test(
    x = b,
    n = b + c,
    p = 0.5
  )
} else {
  message("No discordant pairs available for testing.")
}

# Display the counts
tibble(
  French_below_English_active = b,
  English_below_French_active = c
)



# ============================================================
# Paired community vs heritage comparison
# ============================================================


# Force both possible outcomes to appear in the table

paired_table <- table(
  Community = factor(
    paired_data$Community,
    levels = c(0, 1)
  ),
  Heritage = factor(
    paired_data$Heritage,
    levels = c(0, 1)
  )
)

paired_table

# McNemar test with continuity correction
mcnemar.test(
  paired_table,
  correct = TRUE
)



# Community active, Heritage below threshold
b <- sum(
  paired_data$Community == 1 &
  paired_data$Heritage == 0
)

# Community below threshold, Heritage active
c <- sum(
  paired_data$Community == 0 &
  paired_data$Heritage == 1
)

# Display discordant pairs
tibble(
  Heritage_below_Community_active = b,
  Community_below_Heritage_active = c
)

# Exact McNemar test
if (b + c > 0) {

  exact_result <- binom.test(
    x = b,
    n = b + c,
    p = 0.5
  )

  exact_result

} else {

  message(
    "No discordant pairs: an exact paired test is not informative."
  )

}


#linear mixed effects model for the trilinguals because they have multiple language observations per child


library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(broom.mixed)

# ============================================================
# STEP 1: Prepare trilingual+ data
# ============================================================

trilingual_data <- inactive_language_data %>%
  filter(
    language_group == "Trilinguals+",
    !is.na(is_active),
    !is.na(language_type)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    below_threshold = 1L - is_active,

    language_type = factor(
      as.character(language_type),
      levels = c("Community", "Heritage")
    )
  )

# Check sample sizes and outcome distributions
trilingual_data %>%
  group_by(language_type) %>%
  summarise(
    N_observations = n(),
    N_children = n_distinct(internal_id),
    N_below = sum(below_threshold),
    Percent_below = round(
      100 * mean(below_threshold), 1
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Check that children contribute multiple language observations
trilingual_data %>%
  count(internal_id) %>%
  count(n, name = "N_children")



# ============================================================
# STEP 2: Fit logistic mixed-effects models
# ============================================================

# Null model
trilingual_null <- glmer(
  below_threshold ~
    1 +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = trilingual_data,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa"
  )
)

# Model with language type
trilingual_model <- glmer(
  below_threshold ~
    language_type +
    (1 | internal_id),
  data = trilingual_data,
  family = binomial,
  control = glmerControl(
    optimizer = "bobyqa"
  )
)

# ============================================================
# STEP 3: Compare models
# ============================================================

anova(
  trilingual_null,
  trilingual_model,
  test = "Chisq"
)

# Model coefficients
summary(trilingual_model)




# ============================================================
# STEP 4: Odds ratios and 95% confidence intervals
# ============================================================

trilingual_OR <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  trilingual_model,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE,
  conf.method = "Wald",
  exponentiate = TRUE
)

trilingual_OR





# ============================================================
# STEP 5: Model diagnostics
# ============================================================

# Singularity
isSingular(trilingual_model)

# Convergence messages
trilingual_model@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages

# Random intercept variance
VarCorr(trilingual_model)

# Number of observations and children
nobs(trilingual_model)

n_distinct(trilingual_data$internal_id)
```
